column1: # Author: Lane #1644 (Codex). Individual read-based dispositions; repository LF source and final #1693 composition.

column8: Finite Engine fixture grammar invokes the real stored operation after membership ends, requiring an error and zero captures; it is an executable contract consumer, not an alternate reader.
Independent view oracle requests all three modes and inspects fact identities and result variants; it cannot obtain stored semantics from method presence alone.
Test fault decorator refuses the requested entity category and otherwise calls storage.ReadStored on its issued source, preserving one dispatch owner.
Auth transaction checks its explicit stored declaration and live transaction before calling ReadStored on that same transaction; it never falls through to the parent engine.
System view deliberately constructs absent node/edge facts with system identity in each result mode, after checking live membership. No physical graph is exposed.
Cypher transaction adapter preserves the issued namespace and transaction through ReadStoredInNamespace; unsupported separators or missing transactions refuse.
Manager size view delegates the new operation to its issued Engine. TJ retains counter/accounting representation and publication ownership; no counter forwarding is added here.
Replication view delegates stored reads through ReadStored on its local issued Engine; mutation replication remains its separate exact authority.

This native edge point adapter directly consumes the already selected b.ReadStored leaf in full mode and carries its context/error. Structural discovery belongs to the outer view operation; the typed native call avoids rediscovery inside required point loops and retains the same physical capture owner.

The native stored-node point adapter has an exact typed BadgerEngine and explicitly requests full materialization from b.ReadStored. The outer operation owns structural admission; the native leaf directly consumes captureReadView and the shared stored decoder, preserving errors and absence without a second traversal.
Commit endpoint validation consumes the already captured endpoint fact map, distinguishing current existence, physical tombstone conflict and invalid endpoints without another read.
Commit preparation batches external endpoints through ReadStoredMetadata and combines current existence with the requested physical head; pending nodes are retained by the transaction owner.

Commit conflict validation first checks buffered deletes, revalidates full hidden-edge identity where required, then batches currentEndpointFactsLocked through ReadStored metadata before checking staged operations. Native conflict and commit publication remain the transaction owner; no visible/full fallback answers required endpoint facts.
Deletion order discovery requests stored incident metadata and extracts endpoint IDs, retaining hidden edges without hydrating their properties or vectors.
Order discovery selects metadata for endpoint-only work; callers explicitly requesting the old image use GetStoredEdge, now a full-mode adapter of the same stored operation.

Under the existing complete entity-order hold, endpoint revalidation batches node presence and deleted-node adjacency into one ReadStoredMetadata call. It respects pending nodes/edges and deleted IDs, and a missing required fact or read error refuses commit without hydrating edge payloads.

CDC preparation batches unchanged endpoint labels and explicitly selected NODEKEY properties before commit writes; touched entities retain canonical commit images. Later event construction reads this captured map.
Native deletion authority derives its exact node/edge footprint from stored metadata and carries failures before authority validation; it does not use visible graph filtering.

Dictionary diagnostics scan physical keys and indexes in the existing captured read view, consult the shared marker within that transaction and ask storedReadInTxn for only labels of finished-index mismatch candidates. Partial readiness is not corruption, ACK-only entities are not physical repair candidates, and required fact errors return.

Repair obtains stored endpoint/type metadata and must propagate a failed fact read; ordinary absence or non-unique surviving numeric candidates remain explicit unresolved outcomes. Public required-error and excluded-payload class checks passed.

Dictionary node repair requires a ready label index, requests only StoredMetadataOnly for the lost node and intersects unresolved label-index numeric IDs. It never derives labels from a full body or guesses a mapping while the authoritative label index is rebuilding.
Full result exposes its already owned fact member; this value accessor neither captures nor rereads storage.
Selected result exposes its already owned fact member without materializing excluded body fields.
Public stored operation validates mode and live membership, resolves the declared provider through the common structural cursor, checks request policy, then invokes that exact provider.
Metadata facade fixes the metadata-only mode and checks the payload-free concrete result variant; it never retries a full-body read.
Stored-presence leaf consumes metadata facts and returns their existence with an error channel, without visible lookup or full materialization fallback.

Composite stored view binds a catalog and only requested children, checks complete mode admission before reading, then uses one transform owner for source-qualified current/physical facts. Unlike visible point selection, the stored operation deliberately retains each requested physical source.
Native operation extends captureReadView: its physical transaction, buffered selections and adjacency candidates enter the existing storedReadInTxn kernel before the capture closes.

The stored edge decoder uses one storedEntityView/transaction for body bytes, compact header, reverse endpoint IDs, references and head generation. Selected mode consumes the shared property decoder; full mode calls source.edgeRecord on that same capture, so it cannot use a substituted live dictionary.
Captured node decoder uses the supplied stored entity view, snapshot reference/head and shared envelope grammar; metadata copies labels only, selected/full modes pay their declared payload work.
Node fact references consume #1667 snapshotNodeRef and the same transaction's forward-entry version, avoiding mutable live dictionary lookup.

Native batched kernel resolves physical and pending/buffered variants on one supplied capture, filters moved adjacency candidates, includes endpoint facts, and creates only the requested result variant.

Transaction provider uses its existing pinned snapshot under its mutex, with pending/deleted node and edge maps from that transaction. Unsupported write-behind snapshots refuse instead of reading latest.
Memory provider delegates to its embedded native capture operation; it creates no second read or snapshot authority.

Retained snapshot provider invokes the same batched kernel on the already retained view, enforces prefix, and explicitly refuses overlays whose physical facts the old snapshot protocol cannot represent.
Resident relationship facts copy only identity/type/endpoints in metadata mode; selected keys and full copies are explicit and cancellation-aware.
Edge reference lookup reads its forward dictionary entry and version on the supplied transaction; absent mappings remain zero references and malformed mappings fail.
Capture identity combines the native store identity with the supplied transaction timestamp and transaction ID; Frontier remains reserved for #1676, with no publication state copy.
Resident node facts copy owned ID/labels and pending/buffered head state; selected properties/full node copies are mode-specific and cancellation-aware.
Namespace provider consumes ReadStoredInNamespace on its existing inner source and namespace; it does not invent a capture.
Tracing provider dispatches ReadStored through the common cursor on its actual inner engine and preserves the issued read view.
WAL provider dispatches the same stored operation through the common cursor; it grants no mutation or journal bypass.
Namespace snapshot provider transforms the already retained snapshot through ReadStoredInNamespace; capture time remains the snapshot owner's.
Constraint engine adapter delegates to the same stored operation on its issued engine, retaining mandatory refusal and error behavior.
Bound stored operation delegates ReadStored to its retained issued engine, without another wrapper walk or stored protocol.
Namespace transform prefixes request IDs using the existing namespace projection, invokes the one stored operation, then validates and transforms all logical/physical endpoint facts before delivery.
One result transform owns provenance and ID projection for metadata, selected and full modes, including physical predecessor variants. Invalid endpoints abort rather than filter a partial result.
